clue.text: Bound to record minutes, say, for part of the year

parts.note: to bound is to leap, which is to spring
to time something is to record how many minutes it takes

explanation.surface: Someone leaps to log the minutes of a meeting at some season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'obliged to', but it is the verb meaning leap.
explanation.definitionFit: The season between winter and summer is one portion of the calendar.

clue.text: Family group in Ireland for a month

definitions.meaning: an Irish clan or branch of a family
The usual short form of the ninth month

explanation.definitionFit: An Irish clan is called a sept, and the ninth month is abbreviated the same way.

clue.text: Shout from river rower produced

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
an oar is what rows, and an oarsman is also called an oar

explanation.surface: A cry goes up from someone rowing on a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A roar is a loud bellow, a kind of loud cry.

clue.text: Battled on in a terribly bad financial position for all of us?

definitions.text: bad financial position for all of us?

indicators.note: terribly signals that the words battled on in a are to be thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: The country fought on through a dreadful financial plight shared by everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' is the anagram signal; the definition is cryptic, since the sum a government owes is a debt borne by every citizen.
explanation.definitionFit: A government's borrowing is a liability shared by the whole populace, a poor state of finances for everyone.

clue.text: It'S not said how one can be protected by diplomacy

indicators.note: protected by means the word for one sits inside, shielded by the word for diplomacy

parts.note: tact is diplomacy, skill in handling people
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A remark about how an individual can be shielded by tactful handling of affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means understood or implied without being spoken.

clue.text: Dangerous subject, once my area of interest

parts.note: mine was the old form of my before a vowel, as in 'mine eyes'
a field is someone's area of interest or expertise

explanation.surface: Someone says a risky topic used to be their speciality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once my' is archaic English: 'mine' stood for 'my' in older usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a topic full of hidden hazards is said to be like ground strewn with explosives.

clue.text: Philosophical type saying why I function the wrong way

indicators.note: saying means we hear the word why spoken, giving the letter it sounds like

parts.note: the word why is pronounced like the letter Y

indicators.note: the wrong way means the words I and function are turned back to front

parts.note: to go is to work or function, as a machine does

explanation.surface: A thinker asks why their mind works backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Y (said like 'why') then I GO turned round, OGI.
explanation.definitionFit: A practitioner of Hindu spiritual discipline is a contemplative, philosophical sort.

clue.text: Began and spoke at length without a single drink

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the speech word goes around the drink

parts.note: to orate is to speak at length, pompously
I is the Roman numeral for one, a single unit
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: Someone started off and gave a long speech without touching a drop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, so ORATED wraps IGIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to start or come into being.

clue.text: Supervise exam I give — Latin, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests a different possible arrangement of the letters in I give Latin

explanation.surface: A teacher says they will set a Latin exam, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: To invigilate is to watch over candidates sitting a test.

clue.text: Mould it in places as play material

indicators.note: to mould is to reshape, so the letters of it in places are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Instructions to shape modelling stuff in various spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mould' seems to describe the play material itself but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The modelling clay children shape is a material for play.

clue.text: Centre of Russki events?

indicators.note: centre of says the letters come from the middle of the phrase Russki events

explanation.surface: Asks where the heart of Russian affairs lay.
explanation.walkthrough: The city was the seat of the first Rus state, Kievan Rus, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The city was the capital of medieval Rus, the hub of its history.

clue.text: Concentrating on one affair, and unlikely to marry?

definitions.meaning: fixed on a sole purpose, focused
inclined to stay unwed, read whimsically

explanation.definitionFit: Being wholly focused on one aim is this; jokingly, so is preferring to stay a bachelor.

clue.text: Existing damage

parts.note: damage is slang for what something costs, and existing is being alive, so the phrase is the price of staying alive

explanation.definitionFit: The expense of everyday necessities is the price one pays just to stay alive.

clue.text: Diligence, for example, shown by one who trains players?

definitions.meaning: a diligence was a public coach in France, a horse-drawn passenger vehicle
a coach for stage actors, read playfully

explanation.definitionFit: A diligence was a horse-drawn passenger coach; jokingly, a drama tutor is a theatre trainer.

clue.text: Where junk's found making an impression among boat collection

indicators.note: among means the words for an and impression go inside the word for boat collection

parts.note: a fleet is a group of boats
a mark is an impression left on something

explanation.surface: Somewhere junk turns up, leaving its mark among a group of ships.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'junk' is also a Chinese boat, which suits the fleet in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand bric-a-brac is sold at a street market of that name.

clue.text: Keen to have one's say and take vital treatment

indicators.note: treatment means the letters of take vital are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone eager to speak takes an essential cure.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatty person is eager to speak a lot.

clue.text: Bad ruling — judge questioning without using head

parts.note: in means in power, as the party in office

indicators.note: without using head says the first letter of the word for questioning is dropped

parts.note: curious means inquisitive, questioning

explanation.surface: A poor decision by a judge who asks questions thoughtlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Injurious means harmful, damaging.

clue.text: Object of quest and bother, led by king

indicators.note: led by puts the word for king in front of the word for bother

parts.note: GR is Georgius Rex, King George
to ail is to trouble or bother

explanation.surface: Something sought, plus a nuisance, under a monarch's lead.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy cup sought by Arthur's knights was the goal of their quest.

clue.text: Alice's intended, for instance, to save

definitions.meaning: in A A Milne's poem 'Buckingham Palace', Alice is marrying one of the soldiers at the palace

explanation.walkthrough: In A A Milne's poem, 'Alice is marrying one of the guard', the soldiers at Buckingham Palace.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice's fiancé was a palace sentry; to shield something is to protect it.

clue.text: Verdict showing discrimination

definitions.meaning: good sense in telling things apart

explanation.definitionFit: A court's ruling is this; so is the ability to make sound decisions.

clue.text: Potty Greek character thus providing classical entertainment

parts.note: a chamber pot is a potty, so chamber stands for it
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
sic is Latin for thus

explanation.surface: A crazy Greek fellow thereby lays on some high-brow fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potty' looks like 'crazy' but means a chamber pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Music for a small ensemble is a classical genre to enjoy.

clue.text: Practice in university followed by man of learning

indicators.note: followed by puts the word for man of learning after the letter for university

parts.note: a sage is a wise, learned person

explanation.surface: Custom at a college, with a scholar coming next.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is customary practice.

clue.text: Spent what's earned, about a sovereign

indicators.note: about means the word for what's earned goes around the word for sovereign

parts.note: won is what one has earned, gained
R is Rex or Regina, a sovereign

explanation.surface: Someone splashed out all their earnings on a gold coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign' suggests the gold coin, but it is the monarch, R.
explanation.definitionFit: Worn out means exhausted, used up.

clue.text: Extreme characters in England greatly affected by anxiety

indicators.note: extreme characters means the first and last letters of England and greatly

explanation.surface: In England people are very anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nervous and on edge is a state of anxiety.

clue.text: One bird repelled these others

indicators.note: repelled means the bird word is driven back, read backwards

parts.note: a skua is a predatory seabird

explanation.surface: A single bird drove off the rest of the flock.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the 'others', more birds, defined by reference.
explanation.definitionFit: These are other seabirds, the puffin's relatives, in contrast with the first bird.

clue.text: Stolen and hard to move, as taps may be

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods
taken as written
cold means unfeeling, hard to move emotionally

explanation.surface: Stolen goods are tough to shift, like plumbing fixtures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard to move' looks physical but means unmoved in feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of taps are typically marked for hot and cold water.

clue.text: Heads off what we have no stomach for

indicators.note: heads off means the first letters of what and we are cut away

explanation.surface: Sounds like dismissing what we cannot bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Detesting something means having no appetite for it.

clue.text: Upper hand in special case, note, held by Dickensian heroine

indicators.note: special treatment of case rearranges its letters
held by puts the note inside the heroine's name

parts.note: Nancy is the heroine of Dickens's Oliver Twist
D is a musical note

explanation.surface: Gaining control in a particular legal matter, a memo held by a Dickens character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' signals the anagram of CASE, ASCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascendancy is dominance, having the advantage over others.
